text:
24-hour news summary.

1. OpenAI’s Astra learns to control a robot, paint the Golden Gate Bridge, and improve through repeated attempts (https://t.me/dlmehr/5192)
2. Researchers found that reasoning models generate fractal-like patterns while solving difficult problems (https://t.me/dlmehr/5193)
3. Magic says its new pretraining recipe matches DeepSeek V4 Pro using 50× less compute (https://t.me/dlmehr/5194)
4. Treasury Secretary Bessent says the U.S. cannot pause AI development because China will not (https://t.me/dlmehr/5195)
5. Databricks introduced Proteus, a system for generating specialized GPU kernels across model sizes (https://t.me/dlmehr/5196)
6. NEON announced *Artificial*, a new film starring Andrew Garfield and Yura Borisov (https://t.me/dlmehr/5197)
7. Gradium launched Voice Design, allowing users to create custom voices from text prompts (https://t.me/dlmehr/5198)
8. State Machines launched infrastructure for recreating enterprise apps as parallel agent environments (https://t.me/dlmehr/5199)
9. OUI-1 is presented as an open-weights generative-UI model achieving 71.7% on Generative UI Bench (https://t.me/dlmehr/5200)
10. OpenAI shared an agent-produced solution to the Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize Problem (https://t.me/dlmehr/5201)
11. A report highlights nearly 5,000 Sharif University graduates pursuing PhDs worldwide (https://t.me/dlmehr/5202)
12. Noam Brown says OpenAI’s model used for the Navier–Stokes work is a major advance over today’s LLMs (https://t.me/dlmehr/5203)
13. OpenAI reportedly used 10,000 concurrent agents, illustrating parallel and latent-space scaling (https://t.me/dlmehr/5204)
14. OpenAI launched ChatGPT Images 2.5 with faster generation, improved fidelity, and more consistent edits (https://t.me/dlmehr/5206)
15. Levent Alpöge acknowledged that de-identified product data may have helped improve OpenAI’s models (https://t.me/dlmehr/5207)
16. Aidan Gomez said production-derived synthetic data is reportedly being used to train consumer AI systems (https://t.me/dlmehr/5208)
17. Alexandr Wang launched Muse, an always-on personal AI assistant that can browse and connect to apps (https://t.me/dlmehr/5209)
18. Mark Chen said no human or agent reviewed user data for the Navier–Stokes effort, while de-identified data supports broader product improvement (https://t.me/dlmehr/5210)
19. Anthropic pretraining researcher Jacob Coxon resigned, citing concerns about companies racing toward self-improving superintelligence (https://t.me/dlmehr/5211)

--Hermes
